title: The mangrove nursery experiment
paragraphs: After a storm washed away young mangroves near the estuary, the environmental club at Tanjung Secondary School created a small nursery beside the sports shed. The students hoped to raise 120 replacement seedlings before moving them to the coast. However, the concrete corner they chose trapped afternoon heat, and several leaves began to curl within the first week.

Two student coordinators, Lila and Bimo, investigated the decline. Lila recorded air and water temperatures at three times each day, while Bimo measured salinity and counted new leaf pairs. They sent these measurements to Dr Arun, a coastal ecologist who had advised the school before. He explained that shallow black trays absorbed heat rapidly and suggested that the club compare a cooler location before replacing any plants.

The club moved half the trays to a covered walkway but left the others beside the sports shed. This change reduced midday water temperatures in the moved trays, although it created a new problem: the walkway had no nearby tap. To solve that difficulty, Bimo fixed two water containers to a light trolley. The device allowed students to refill every tray without carrying open buckets through busy corridors.

After six weeks, the seedlings from the covered walkway had produced more new leaf pairs. The club then transferred sixty healthy plants to the estuary and kept sixty in the nursery. The first group was planted behind a line of old mangrove roots that slowed the waves; the second remained at school as a comparison group. This arrangement let the students separate the effect of the estuary from ordinary growth over time.

During the first month, the estuary seedlings grew more slowly than those at school, but a later storm damaged very few of them. That finding persuaded the club to continue using old roots as shelter during future planting. By the end of term, what had begun as an emergency rescue had become a repeatable method: measure conditions, test one change, keep a comparison group and move seedlings only when the evidence supports it.
